       ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA TRANSMISSION
      SERVICES CORPORATION’S NOTICE OF COMPLIANCE WITH PREHEARING
            SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS IN SOAH ORDER NOS. 6 AND 23

        Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (“Oncor”) and LCRA Transmission Services

Corporation (“LCRA TSC,” and together with Oncor, “Applicants”), hereby file this notice of

compliance with the prehearing submission requirements set out in State Office of Administrative

Hearings (“SOAH”) Order No. 6, issued on April 20, 2026, and SOAH Order No. 23, issued on May

29, 2026.

                                         I.      INTRODUCTION

        Among other things, SOAH Order No. 6 adopted a procedural schedule, set a date for the

hearing on the merits (“Hearing”), and established certain record requirements and deadlines for

presentation in the Hearing. 1



1
  See generally SOAH Order No. 6 – Memorializing Prehearing Conference; Granting Request for Good-Cause Exception
to Filing Requirements; Extending Deadline for Comments on Sufficiency of Application and Notice; Adopting
Procedural Schedule; Setting Route Adequacy Hearing, Prehearing Conference, and Hearing on the Merits; Addressing
Hearing Procedures; and Providing Advisory to Intervenors Regarding Potential Dismissal (Apr. 20, 2026) (Item No.
788).

APPLICANTS’ NOTICE OF COMPLIANCE WITH PREHEARING
SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS IN SOAH ORDER NOS. 6 AND 23                                         Page 1 of 6
                                                                                                              1
         SOAH Order No. 6 established the following deadlines:

   i.   As soon as practicable, Applicants must: (1) retain a court-reporting service to transcribe the

        Hearing and notify the other parties of the service that was retained; and (2) notify the court-

        reporting service that the parties will exchange exhibits using either an electronic repository

        provided by Applicants that the court reporter will also be able to access or filings on the

        Public Utility Commission of Texas’ (“PUC’s” or the “Commission’s”) Interchange.

 ii.    By June 3, 2026, Applicants must file:

            a. a list of persons who have signed the Protective Order adopted in this proceeding; and

            b. a proposed order of presentation, witnesses, and cross-examination for the Hearing.

 iii.   By June 3, 2026, each party must submit electronic copies of the following to SOAH, the

        other parties, and the court reporter:

            a. a witness list (identifying all witnesses the party intends to call to testify during the

                Hearing, listed in the order that the party intends to call them);

            b. an exhibit list (identifying all exhibits the party intends to offer at the Hearing known

                prior to the Hearing); and

            c. all exhibits included on the party’s exhibit list.

        SOAH Order No. 23 directed Applicants to file a spreadsheet, in native format, listing all

intervenors, grouped by route segments to the extent possible. The ALJs advised that this list shall

serve as the basis for the proposed order of cross-examination and presentation at the hearing. 2

        With this notice and Applicants’ prior actions described below, Applicants have complied

with the pre-hearing record requirements under SOAH Order Nos. 6 and 23.




2
  SOAH Order No. 23 – Requiring Applicant Filing and Denying Motion for Additional Pre-Hearing Conference (May
29, 2026) (Item No. 5248).

APPLICANTS’ NOTICE OF COMPLIANCE WITH PREHEARING
SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS IN SOAH ORDER NOS. 6 AND 23                                       Page 2 of 6
                                                                                                            2
                 II.     COMPLIANCE WITH PREHEARING REQUIREMENTS

   i.   Court Reporter and Electronic Repository – Applicants engaged Kennedy Reporting Service

        to transcribe the Hearing. Questions for the court reporter can be directed to:

        order@kennedyreporting.com. In accordance with party communications regarding electronic

        file-sharing, Applicants provided the parties of record with information and instructions

        relating to electronic submissions and access. Applicants notified Kennedy Reporting Service

        that the parties will exchange exhibits electronically and provided the court reporter with

        access to the appropriate folders on Egnyte, the file sharing repository provided by Applicants

        for this proceeding.

 ii.    Protective Order Log – Included as Attachment 1 hereto is a log that lists all persons that, on

        behalf of a current party in this case, have signed Protective Order certifications in this

        proceeding.

 iii.   Proposed Order of Presentation – Applicants propose the following order of presentation at

        the Hearing:

            a. Applicants;

            b. Intervenors, grouped by route segment, in the order listed in Attachment 2 pursuant to

                SOAH Order No. 23;

            c. Office of Public Utility Counsel (OPUC);

            d. Commission Staff.

 iv.    Presentation of Witnesses – Due to the number of witnesses appearing on behalf of Applicants,

        and as a result of SOAH Order No. 12 3 granting partial consolidation of this docket with




3
  SOAH Order No. 12 – In Docket No. 59475 Denying Motion for Continuance and Granting in Part Motion to
Consolidate May 8, 2026) (Item No. 3718).

          Docket No. 59182 on the issue of need, Applicants propose to have two witness panel

         presentations—the first on the issue of need, the second on the issue of routing. First,

         Applicants propose to present their witnesses supporting the issue of need as a panel on direct

         and rebuttal at the same time unless cross-examination of these witnesses is waived by all

         other parties. Applicants’ witnesses that will comprise the panel on need are: Jared Gurley,

         P.E. and Collin M. Martin, P.E. All parties will have the opportunity to cross-examine

         Applicants’ panel on need in accordance with the order of presentation in Attachment 2. Upon

         conclusion of the need panel, the second panel will be presented on the issue of routing. With

         the exception of Applicants’ witness Dr. Edward P. Gelmann, Applicants propose to present

         their witnesses supporting the issue of routing as a panel on direct and rebuttal at the same

         time unless cross-examination of these witness is waived by all other parties. Applicants’

         witnesses that will comprise the panel on routing are: Casey D. Petty, Russell Marusak,

         Corin E. Cooley, P.E., KayLynne Phillips, Kelly Wells, and Dave Elliott. All parties will

         have the opportunity to cross-examine Applicants’ panel on routing in accordance with the

         order of presentation in Attachment 2. Finally, Applicants propose to present their witness Dr.

         Edward P. Gelmann as a standalone witness that will appear virtually on June 10th, 11th, or

         12th, 2026. 4 Dr. Gelmann will also be subject to cross-examination in accordance with the

         proposed order of presentation in Attachment 2.

    v.   Applicants’ Cross-Examination Witness List – Included hereto as Attachment 3 is a list of

         witnesses Applicants are designating for cross-examination at the Hearing at this time.

 vi.   Exhibits and Exhibit List - Attachment 4 hereto is a list of exhibits that Applicants intend to

       offer into evidence at the Hearing. Applicants uploaded Attachment 4 to Egnyte and to

       Kiteworks, SOAH’s electronic file-sharing site. Applicants do not currently have cross-

       examination or re-direct exhibits. Applicants reserve the right to offer additional exhibits

       responsive to live testimony elicited, and arguments made, by other parties at the Hearing.

                                      III.    CONCLUSION

Applicants respectfully submit this notice of compliance with all prehearing record requirements

ordered by the presiding officers in this proceeding.
